newsitem.title: CHINA: Everbright Int'l in 1-for-4 rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Everbright Int'l in 1-for-4 rights issue.

text.p: China Everbright International Ltd announced a one-for-four rights issue which will result in the issue of 400.30 million new shares and raise about HK$840 million, the company said in an announcement on Monday.
Most of the proceeds will be invested in two Shanghai property development projects to be acquired from its parent company China Everbright Holdings, the announcement said.

The rights shares would be issued at HK$2.10 per share and account for about 25 percent of the existing issued share capital of the company and 20 percent of the enlarged issued capital, the statement said.
Assuming all rights are taken up, the company will raise about HK$840 million before expenses, it said.
Trading in the shares, which was suspended on Friday, resumed on Monday. The share was trading HK$0.30 lower at HK$5.00 at mid-morning.

The funds will be used to acquire a 25 percent stake in Hong Kong Shanghai Development Co Ltd, the developer of a property known as Kerry Everbright City, for a total of HK$574 million, the statement said.

Kerry Everbright City comprised 11 lots with a total site area of 64,274 square metres and was planned to be developed into a commercial and residential complex in several phases. Only phase I, which was scheduled for completion in August 1997, was under development, the statement said.
Kerry Everbright City had been valued in its present state of development at HK$3.28 billion as at end June 1997. A 25 percent stake in the project would be equal to HK$820 million.
The acquisition cost of HK$574 million represented a discount of 30 percent to the market value of the controlling shareholder's proportionate interest in the property, it said.
Everbright International would also acquire a 15 percent stake in Kerry Shanghai (Hongkou) Ltd from its controlling shareholder for a total HK$25 million.
The principal asset of Kerry Shanghai was the Shanghai Trade Square/International Apartments, completed in October 1996, and valued at HK$280 million as at May 31, 1997.
The acquisition price represented a discount of 30 percent to the market value of the proportionate interest in the property, the statement said.
Of the HK$840 million raised in the rights issue, HK$603 million would be used to acquire the Shanghai properties and the balance would be used as general working capital, the statement said.
China Everbright Holdings has a 62.2 percent stake in Everbright International.
